newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas rises amid shortcovering, firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas rises amid shortcovering, firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures edged higher in Tuesday morning trade amid shortcovering and talk of firmer cash prices, industry sources said.

At 1110 EST, May rose 5.4 cents to $1.895 per mmBtu but remained stuck in recent ranges, reluctant to retest the $1.91 support level. June climbed four cents to $1.94, while other deferreds were mostly higher.

"It's a good value down here. A lot of people are short the market. Maybe they're trying to scare the shorts out," one Houston-based trader said, noting the rising heating oil futures and cash market may also be sparking the uptick.

Technically, traders said there was support in May at Monday's low of $1.825, and then at $1.78 and $1.68. Resistance was seen at $1.91, and then at $1.93-1.94 and last Thursday's high of $1.97. Further resistance was pegged at $2.04-2.05.
As of 1035 EST, NYMEX said 3,567 Hub contracts had traded.

In the cash market, Gulf prices for Wednesday were steady to higher at $1.86-1.89 at the Henry Hub. April prices at the hub rose several cents to $1.82-1.86. Swing prices on the Midcontinent pipes were up about two cents to the mid-to-high $1.70s, while April was equally higher in the low-to-mid $1.70s.
Most traders attributed the price uptick to storage buying in the producing and western regions.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 30 to 50 bcf, compared with 43 bcf a year ago.

Temperatures throughout most of the U.S., excluding the northernmost plains, are forecast to average above normal Wednesday through the end of the week. In the Southwest, forecasts over the next several days are calling for temperatures to average four degrees above normal northwest, 12 degrees above normal northeast and five degrees above normal south. Cooler weather is expected for the weekend in the East and Midwest, Weather Services Corp said.
As of 1113 EST, no Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On the KCBT, April gained four cents to $1.72 ahead of its expiry later today. Deferreds were flat to up seven cents. Open interest for March 24 dropped 246 lots to 3,118.
Physical prices in the Permian basin were talked steady to higher in the low-$1.70s. April 1 deals were reported done at $1.67-1.70, showing a gain of more than five cents from Monday.
